issues.title: Sign error in the prior covariance
issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines Delta e_j=-lambda_j e_j with lambda_j>0. Hence Delta^{-gamma} is not a positive real covariance for the admitted general gamma (and is negative for odd integer gamma), whereas the Gaussian series uses positive eigenvalues lambda_j^{-gamma}.
issues.overall_effect: As literally written, the specific Gaussian prior used by the reaction-diffusion main theorem is not a valid covariance operator for all allowed gamma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the covariance rho^2 Delta^(-gamma) by rho^2(-Delta)^(-gamma) on the mean-zero subspace. No proof or downstream statement otherwise needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The old source itself uniquely forces this correction: it defines Delta e_j=-lambda_j e_j and then represents the same prior using the positive variances lambda_j^(-gamma). Inserting the missing minus sign only reconciles malformed notation, and no mathematical inference relies on the literal sign.

issues.title: Missing dimension factor in spectral projection rates
issues.failure_explanation: Since lambda_J is comparable to J^{2/d}, an H^gamma tail has L2 rate lambda_J^{-gamma/2}, hence J^{-gamma/d}, not J^{-gamma}. For d>1, taking phi=e_{J+1} gives left side one while the old right side is of order J^{-gamma(1-1/d)}, which tends to zero. The sharp RKHS projection growth is correspondingly J^{(gamma-r)/d}.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed approximation claim is false for the admissible dimensions d=2,3, and the old projection-error and Cameron-Martin rate calculations do not establish the Laplace approximation and ensuing BvM chain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the projection bounds by the dimension-correct rates J^(-gamma/d) and max(1,J^((gamma-r)/d)). Then reoptimize the J_N-dependent localization and Cameron-Martin calculations—for example, keep J_N comparable to N delta_N^2, use K_N=sqrt(J_N) max(1,J_N^((gamma-kappa)/d)), establish localization through finite-dimensional covering of the projected Sobolev ball, and redo all projection-remainder and shift estimates with the corrected exponents. This recovers the Laplace approximation and every listed BvM consequence under the stated hypotheses.
issues.why_classification: For d=2,3 the old estimate makes a genuinely false rate claim, and merely editing its exponent does not repair the dependent proof because the localization, approximation remainders, and Cameron-Martin bounds all use that rate. A contained but nontrivial cutoff and entropy reoptimization recovers the existing proof architecture and all theorem-level guarantees, while the corrected spectral estimate remains recognizably comparable. Thus the issue exceeds minor but requires neither global reconstruction nor major mathematical loss.

issues.title: Uniform-design Hilbert-space normalization

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the $X_i$ are drawn iid from the uniform distribution $\lambda$ on $\mathcal X = [0,T] \times \Omega$

issues.failure_explanation: The prose specifies a uniform probability design on a cylinder of Lebesgue volume T, so lambda=dt dx/T. The old convention instead equips L2(X) and the adjoint with the unnormalized dt dx inner product. Consequently the empirical score variance and likelihood curvature contain a factor 1/T that is absent from the Gaussian exponent in laplaceapp. The discrepancy changes the exact limiting covariance for T not equal to one, rather than merely changing an implicit inequality constant.
issues.overall_effect: For a general observation horizon T, the old BvM chain identifies a Gaussian covariance with the wrong nonvanishing normalization factor, although qualitative rates are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the probability-design measure lambda=dt dx/T throughout the statistical argument. Define the observation-space inner product, adjoint, information operator, inverse-information directions, Laplace quadratic term, and limiting Gaussian covariance in L^2_lambda, or equivalently insert the resulting fixed T-rescalings consistently through all listed dependent results.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine normalization error because the old score and curvature calculation uses the wrong measure, so it is not merely typographical. Nevertheless, the repair is routine fixed-scalar bookkeeping: it changes no hypotheses, model class, rate, proof method, or qualitative BvM guarantee, and only corrects the exact normalization of the limiting covariance.

issues.title: Wrong variance order in empirical-process chaining
issues.failure_explanation: For the linearisation remainder g, Condition B gives at most a first-order L2 bound and hence the displayed second-power variance bound. With sigma_N then first order in the contraction radius, the subsequent rate stated in the old proof does not follow. Condition C instead gives ||g||_{L2} bounded by the squared parameter distance, so Ef^2 is bounded by its fourth power, exactly the variance order used later.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not establish that the stochastic linearisation remainder is o(1), leaving the posterior Laplace approximation and BvM chain unsupported by this argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For q=theta-theta_0-(t/sqrt(N))p_N(bar psi), invoke Condition C rather than Condition B to obtain ||g||_{L^2} at most C||q||_{L^2}^2. Consequently Ef_{theta,psi}^2 is at most C||q||_{L^2}^4 and sigma_N^2 is of order tilde-delta_N(zeta)^4+N^(-2). Substitution of this variance into the existing chaining calculation gives the required o(1) bound and restores the Laplace and BvM chain.
issues.why_classification: Condition C in the old source already supplies exactly the quadratic remainder estimate needed, and the subsequent displayed chaining rate is the one corresponding to its fourth-power variance. Correcting the invoked condition and variance order is a short, local, routine repair with unchanged assumptions and conclusions, though it repairs an invalid inference and therefore is not a typo.

issues.title: Non-regular mean-value selector
issues.failure_explanation: For each point, the scalar mean-value theorem only asserts existence of some intermediate value; it gives no measurable, let alone C^1, dependence of the selected s on (t,x). Treating the resulting tilde u as a regular convex combination therefore does not establish that V=f'(tilde u) satisfies the C^1([0,T],C^1) hypothesis used by paristexas.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof of the nonlinear stability condition E for the reaction-diffusion map is incomplete, so its use in the reaction-diffusion BvM theorem is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pointwise mean-value selector by the exact averaged potential V(t,x)=integral from 0 to 1 of f'(u_{theta_0}(t,x)+s(u_theta(t,x)-u_{theta_0}(t,x))) ds. Then f(u_theta)-f(u_{theta_0})=V(u_theta-u_{theta_0}); differentiating under the integral and applying the existing uniform regularity bounds gives the required C^1([0,T],C^1) bound, so the stability lemma and both dependent BvM results apply.
issues.why_classification: The old proof incorrectly assigns regularity to an arbitrary pointwise mean-value choice, so mathematical repair is required. The integral divided-difference formula is a standard local replacement, and its regularity follows directly from estimates already proved in the source; it introduces no new assumption, weakened regime, or nontrivial proof architecture.

issues.title: Quadratic linearisation remainder proof
issues.failure_explanation: Writing w=u_{theta_0+h}-u_{theta_0}, Taylor's formula gives |m| bounded by a constant times |w|^2, so its L2 norm requires an L4 bound on w; the available estimate tbdu controls only the L2 norm. Thus the displayed bound of the L2 norm of m by the squared L2 norm of w is unjustified and the old proof does not establish the quadratic remainder.
issues.overall_effect: The reaction-diffusion verification of the quadratic linearisation condition, and consequently the reaction-diffusion BvM application, were not established by the old proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let w=u_{theta_0+h}-u_{theta_0}. Derive from the difference equation the energy estimate sup_t||w(t)||_{L^2}^2+integral_0^T||w(t)||_{H^1}^2 dt at most C||h||_{L^2}^2. For the Taylor source m, use d<=3 and H^1 embedding into L^4 to obtain ||m(t)||_{H^(-1)} at most C||w(t)||_{L^2}||w(t)||_{H^1}. A direct energy estimate for the zero-initial-value remainder equation then gives sup_t||r(t)||_{L^2}^2 at most C integral_0^T||m(t)||_{H^(-1)}^2 dt, hence at most C||h||_{L^2}^4. Taking square roots proves the stated quadratic linearisation bound and restores both dependent results.
issues.why_classification: The false L^2 product estimate cannot be fixed by a notation change or by directly reusing tbdu. Recovering the same quadratic guarantee requires a different negative-Sobolev forcing estimate together with an additional integrated H^1 energy bound. This is a contained but nontrivial replacement argument that preserves the theorem and downstream BvM guarantees, so it is moderate rather than serious.
